title: Build Your Personal E‑Portfolio: Why It Matters and a Step‑by‑Step Guide (Workshop)
excerpt: Practical workshop: choose from ready‑made GitHub templates, customize in Windsurf, preview with Live Server, enable GitHub Copilot, and publish via GitHub Pages.
html:
Your e‑portfolio is your always‑on intro. In this workshop we’ll build a fast, accessible site, using AI to speed up while keeping control over the content—no code snippets here, just the templates and steps you’ll use.

Why an e‑portfolio

  • Credibility: Control what people see first.
  • Context: Show problem → approach → outcome.
  • Compounding: One canonical place to publish projects/posts.

Starter templates (pick one)

  • webtemp4 — GitHub • Live demo
  • website5 — GitHub • Live demo
  • webite6 — GitHub • Live demo
  • tech-1-template — GitHub
  • tech-2-template — GitHub
  • general-template — GitHub
  • art-template — GitHub

Tools we’ll use

  • Cursor (AI editor): download
  • Windsurf (AI IDE): download
  • GitHub Education + Copilot: apply and enable Copilot
  • Live Server (VS Code): extension
  • Git & GitHub for publishing (GitHub Pages)

Step‑by‑step

  1. Install Windsurf (or Cursor): Use the link(s) above and sign in.
  2. Choose a template: Open one of the GitHub repos here and click Use this template (or Download ZIP).
  3. Open in Windsurf/VS Code: Personalize the text, images, and links to your own projects.
  4. Enable GitHub Education + Copilot: Turn on Copilot in your editor for faster edits and refactors.
  5. Preview locally: Install the Live Server extension and open index.html with it to see changes instantly.
  6. Push to GitHub: Create a repo on GitHub and use your preferred UI (GitHub Desktop or VS Code Source Control) to publish.
  7. Publish with GitHub Pages: In your repo, go to Settings → Pages → set Source to Deploy from a branch and pick main (root). Optionally add a custom domain via the Pages settings.

Tips

  • Replace placeholder images and compress them for speed.
  • Check accessibility basics: readable contrast, alt text, focus states.
  • Keep your homepage copy crisp: who you are, what you build, and links.

AI Portfolio Prompts

Copy one prompt below into your AI assistant (Copilot Chat, Claude, Gemini, ChatGPT, etc.). Replace bracketed placeholders like [YOUR NAME], [EMAIL], [GITHUB]. Each prompt requests a structured, responsive, accessible personal website with clear sections.

Prompt 1: Mathematics Student
I am a mathematics student at Mercer County Community College. Please generate a modern, responsive personal website with:
- Hero section (my name, concise tagline, links to GitHub + LinkedIn)
- Projects section (calculus visualization tool, statistics project, research assistant experience) each with problem → approach → outcome
- Experience & Leadership (tutoring, math club officer, volunteer roles)
- Skills (math topics, programming languages, tools)
- A resume upload/download placeholder
- Contact form
Ensure accessible color contrast, semantic HTML, and easy future expansion. Provide clear TODO comments where I should insert real project details.

Prompt 2: CS Sophomore Seeking Internship
I am a sophomore Computer Science student seeking a Summer 2026 software engineering internship. Build a portfolio with:
Sections: About, Skills (Python, Java, C++, JS), Projects (cards with tags + GitHub links), Hackathons & Open Source contributions, Experience, Leadership (clubs), Blog template placeholder, Resume (download button), Contact form.
Include a dark/light mode toggle and clear CTAs. Use semantic HTML, ARIA where helpful, and mark placeholders.

Prompt 3: Data Analytics Transfer Student
I am a data analytics transfer student focusing on predictive modeling and research posters. Create a site with:
- Summary hero (name, focus areas: forecasting, visualization)
- Project gallery (dataset summaries, modeling approach, metrics)
- Research & Posters section
- Certifications (Google Data Analytics, others)
- Interactive charts placeholder area
- Resume section + contact form
Optimize for performance and accessibility. Indicate where to embed interactive charts later.

Prompt 4: Cybersecurity Bootcamp Graduate
I completed a cybersecurity bootcamp. Build a portfolio with:
- Hero (name, tagline: Defensive & Offensive Security Learner)
- Labs & Write‑ups (penetration test practice, network hardening, incident response) each card links to a detailed page
- Certifications (Security+, CEH in progress, TryHackMe badges) section
- Homelab architecture diagram placeholder
- PGP public key block + contact form
- Resume download
Add clear security-themed styling, good contrast, and semantic HTML.

Prompt 5: Nursing Student Pivoting to Health Informatics
I am a nursing student transitioning to health informatics. Generate a site with:
- Intro (clinical background + informatics pivot)
- Clinical Experience timeline
- Informatics Projects (EHR workflow analysis, medication safety app concept) with problem → improvement
- Skills matrix (clinical vs technical)
- HIPAA compliance disclaimer section
- Resume and contact form
Accessible, calm color palette; mark all placeholders.

Prompt 6: Veteran Transitioning to Tech
I am a veteran transitioning to software engineering. Build a portfolio featuring:
- Hero (service background → software focus)
- Timeline (military roles, training, GI Bill education path)
- Projects (mission‑critical inspired apps, logistics tool) with outcomes
- Leadership & Teamwork highlights
- Skills (languages, tools, soft skills)
- Resume + Contact
Emphasize professionalism, accessibility, and semantic structure.

Prompt 7: UX/UI Designer Student
I am a UX/UI student. Create a site with:
- Hero (name, specialization, CTA to case studies)
- Case Studies (problem, research, wireframes, usability metrics, outcomes)
- Design Process page
- Accessibility statement section
- Figma embeds placeholder area
- Resume + scheduling link (Calendly placeholder)
Provide consistent spacing, typography scale, and ARIA landmarks.

Prompt 8: AI/ML Enthusiast
I am an AI/ML enthusiast. Build a site with:
- Hero (name, focus areas: NLP, CV, MLOps)
- Experiment Gallery (interactive demo placeholders, model cards with metrics)
- Publications / Articles section
- Tech Stack & Tools
- Data Ethics statement
- Resume + Contact form
Include spots for embedding iframes (Gradio/Streamlit) later.

Prompt 9: Business Analytics Student
I am a business analytics student. Create a portfolio with:
- Hero (name, tagline: Turning Data into Actionable Insight)
- Dashboard Showcase (placeholder images with KPI commentary)
- Internship Experience summaries
- Certifications (Tableau, Power BI, Excel)
- Projects (case study cards)
- Resume + newsletter subscription form
Ensure responsive grid and accessible charts placeholders.

Prompt 10: Creative Technologist (3D + Web)
I combine 3D design and web development. Build a site with:
- Hero (name, quick pitch)
- 3D Gallery (WebGL / Three.js placeholder components)
- Process Journal (chronological entries)
- Collaborations section
- Tech & Tools
- Resume + inquiry form
Add dark/light theme toggle and note where I insert actual WebGL embeds.

title: Git & GitHub: A Beginner’s Guide with Essential Commands
excerpt: Start version control in minutes: install Git, configure, commit, branch, and push to GitHub with the most-used commands.
html:
Version control lets you track changes, experiment safely, and collaborate. This quick guide gets you productive with Git and GitHub using the most common commands.

Install and configure Git

Download: git-scm.com/downloads

git --version

# Your identity
git config --global user.name "Your Name"
git config --global user.email "you@example.com"

# Defaults (recommended)
git config --global init.defaultBranch main
# Windows: normalize line endings
git config --global core.autocrlf true

Initialize a new repository

mkdir my-project && cd my-project
git init

echo "# My Project" > README.md


git status
# Stage and commit your first file
git add README.md
git commit -m "Initial commit"

Clone a repository

git clone https://github.com/OWNER/REPO.git
cd REPO

Everyday Git workflow

# See what changed
git status

# Stage changes
git add <file>        # stage one file
git add .               # stage everything modified/new

# Save a snapshot
git commit -m "Describe your change"

# Inspect history & changes
git log --oneline --graph --decorate --all
git diff                 # unstaged changes
git diff --staged        # staged changes

# Undo (safe & common)
git restore <file>           # discard unstaged changes
git restore --staged <file>  # unstage

# Move / delete tracked files
git mv old-name new-name
git rm path/to/file

Branching and merging

# Create and switch to a new branch
git switch -c feature/idea

# List branches
git branch

# Switch back to main
git switch main

# Merge a finished feature into main
git merge feature/idea

Sync with GitHub remotes

Create a repository on GitHub, then connect and push:

# Add a remote named "origin"
git remote add origin https://github.com/USER/REPO.git
# or SSH: git remote add origin git@github.com:USER/REPO.git

# Verify remotes
git remote -v

# First push (sets upstream)
git push -u origin main

# Get latest changes
git pull                 # fetch + merge current branch
git fetch origin         # fetch without merging

# Push a feature branch
git push -u origin feature/idea

Stash work-in-progress

git stash push -m "wip: refactor"
git stash list
git stash pop

Tag releases

git tag v1.0.0
git push origin v1.0.0

Ignore files with .gitignore

echo "node_modules/" >> .gitignore
git rm -r --cached node_modules
git commit -m "Add .gitignore"

Get help

git help <command>
git <command> -h

Docs: Git • GitHub
